cards.claim: Adaptive selection of Newton–Schulz iteration depth (via spectral estimation) can reduce validation loss below fixed-depth Muon baselines across all fixed depths
cards.conditions: GPT-style decoder-only models, 160M parameters, Nemotron-CC v2 High-Quality dataset, Muon optimizer, B tokens pretraining
cards.effect: With 5 iterations, spectral-adaptive method reaches lower validation loss than fixed baseline at any fixed depth (2–7 iterations)
cards.evidence: Experimental results from Table 4 and pretraining runs
cards.quote: With only five iterations, our method reaches a lower loss than the fixed baseline at any depth, so adaptation can replace extra iterations.

cards.claim: Spectral estimation-based Newton–Schulz adaptation improves validation loss in Muon across model scales without extra per-step cost
cards.conditions: GPT pretraining on Nemotron-CC v2 High-Quality, 160M/300M/1B parameter models, B tokens, spectral estimation every K steps with fixed-depth RMS rule
cards.effect: Consistent improvement over fixed conservative PE baseline at all model sizes tested
cards.evidence: End-to-end pretraining experiments, Table 3 (final validation loss)
cards.quote: Spectral estimation improves on the fixed baseline for both optimizers at every model size, and it matches or improves on periodic selection from an exact SVD or eigendecomposition ( Tables 4 and 8 ).
